title: Complex Langevin kernels for real-time SU(N) lattice gauge theory in 3+1 dimensions
summary: We investigate complex Langevin (CL) dynamics for real-time SU($N$) gauge theories in 3+1 dimensions and introduce new kernel modifications tailored for lattice gauge theory (LGT). Using the anisotropic kernel as a baseline, we demonstrate that on a rectangular regularized Schwinger-Keldysh time contour, stable simulations are possible for pure SU(2) gauge theory up to a real-time extent of $2β$ at a bare coupling $g=0.5$, where $β$ denotes the inverse temperature. We show that a contour-dependent phase kernel extends this reach to $3β$, while a local, field-dependent kernel based on traced plaquettes achieves $3.5β$. These constructions represent the first application of such kernels to LGTs, especially in 3+1 dimensions. To validate the approach, we generalize the CL correctness criterion based on the drift magnitude to kernelled dynamics, providing a practical tool to assess correct convergence. Our results substantially advance the applicability of CL to real-time simulations in Minkowski space, establishing a framework for controlled studies of non-Abelian gauge theories at unprecedented time scales. A forthcoming paper applies these developments to the computation of unequal-time correlation functions.

AI.tldr: The paper advances the use of complex Langevin dynamics in 3+1 dimensional real-time SU(N) gauge theories, introducing new kernel modifications for lattice gauge theory. It shows stable simulations up to a real-time extent of 3.5β and provides a correctness criterion for these simulations, paving the way for studies of non-Abelian gauge theories at longer time scales.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to improve and extend the applicability of complex Langevin (CL) dynamics for simulating real-time SU(N) gauge theories, particularly in 3+1 dimensions, by developing new kernel modifications that can lead to stable simulations over longer real-time extents and at higher temperatures.
AI.method: The authors employ anisotropic kernels as a baseline and introduce contour-dependent phase kernels and field-dependent kernels based on traced plaquettes to enhance the stability of CL simulations. They also generalize the CL correctness criterion to assess the convergence of the modified dynamics.
AI.result: The results show that with the new kernel modifications, stable simulations are possible for pure SU(2) gauge theory up to a real-time extent of 3.5β at a bare coupling g=0.5. The generalized correctness criterion validates the approach and its application to the simulations.
AI.conclusion: The study significantly advances the ability to apply CL to real-time simulations in Minkowski space, providing a robust framework for future controlled studies of non-Abelian gauge theories, including the computation of unequal-time correlation functions.

title: Agentic AI for QCD perturbation theory or: how I learned to stop worrying and love the bot
comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, presented at the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026) July 26 to August 1, 2026 University of Maryland, College Park, USA
summary: AI coding agents are extremely effective at performing calculations that can be broken down into modular steps, each with verifiable checks of correctness. Perturbative QCD calculations satisfy both of these properties and we find that they are well-suited to solution by agentic AI systems. We discuss our methods for instructing and verifying the work of agents in one- and two-loop perturbative calculations, with a focus on pre-empting common mistakes. We find that once an agent has successfully completed one perturbative calculation, its instructions transfer very well to other similar calculations which can then be completed and verified in a matter of hours with little effort from the user.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the effectiveness of AI coding agents in performing perturbative QCD calculations, which are well-structured and verifiable. The authors share their methods for guiding and verifying the work of these agents, noting that after an initial successful calculation, the same instructions can be effectively applied to similar calculations with minimal user effort.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to leverage the capabilities of AI coding agents for performing complex but modular and verifiable calculations, specifically in the domain of perturbative QCD, thereby reducing human effort and time required for such tasks.
AI.method: The method involves developing and applying specific instructions to guide AI coding agents through one- and two-loop perturbative calculations. A key focus is on setting up checks to prevent common errors and ensure the correctness of each step in the process.
AI.result: The results indicate that once an AI agent has been successfully guided through a single perturbative calculation, it can then apply the learned instructions to other similar calculations efficiently, completing them within hours and with little additional oversight.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion suggests that AI coding agents are highly effective for perturbative QCD calculations, with the potential for significant time savings and reduced error rates. The transferability of the initial set of instructions across similar calculations highlights the scalability of this approach.

title: Hot and dense QCD equation of state from the complex Langevin equation
comment: 4 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea
summary: We discuss the QCD equation of state at temperatures above the crossover and for high baryon chemical potentials, obtained via the first ever complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass. In particular, we present continuum-extrapolated results for the energy, entropy, and enthalpy densities, as well as for the specific heat capacity as a function of baryon chemical potential and temperature.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the QCD equation of state at high temperatures and baryon chemical potentials, using complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass, with continuum-extrapolated thermodynamic quantities.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to explore the QCD equation of state in a regime that is difficult to access with traditional lattice QCD methods, specifically at non-zero baryon density, which is important for understanding the behavior of matter under extreme conditions such as those found in neutron stars or heavy-ion collisions.
AI.method: The method involves performing complex Langevin simulations, which are capable of handling the sign problem that arises in lattice QCD at finite baryon chemical potential, and extrapolating the results to the continuum limit to obtain physical predictions.
AI.result: The results include continuum-extrapolated values for energy, entropy, and enthalpy densities, as well as the specific heat capacity, all as functions of both baryon chemical potential and temperature, providing insights into the thermodynamics of QCD matter.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion is that complex Langevin simulations at the physical pion mass can successfully be used to determine the QCD equation of state at high baryon chemical potentials, giving a better understanding of the phase structure and thermodynamics of QCD at these conditions.

title: Enhanced Signal and Excited-State Control in Nonlocal Lattice Correlators
summary: Nonlocal correlation functions underpin lattice calculations of parton physics. However, their extraction is limited by a rapidly deteriorating signal-to-noise ratio with increasing Euclidean separation and hadron momentum, and by excited-state contamination. We propose a new fitting strategy that enhances control over both: by taking the ratio of nonlocal to local correlators, we can project out the dominant ground-state dynamics with a signal that is much cleaner and far less sensitive to excited states than the conventional approach. We demonstrate the method on the quark and gluon PDF, the quark GPD and TMDPDF. The results are consistent with those from the conventional three-point/two-point ratio fit but exhibit markedly improved precision and stability, and extend the accessible range to larger hadron momenta. For nonforward matrix elements such as GPDs, our strategy greatly simplifies the analysis procedure. Our method applies to general Dirac and momentum structures, for connected and disconnected contributions, and extends naturally to other nonlocal correlators, making it immediately deployable in existing lattice programs toward precision hadron structure.

AI.tldr: A new fitting strategy is proposed for enhancing the accuracy and stability of nonlocal correlation functions in lattice calculations, which are crucial for parton physics. This method, applicable to a wide range of correlators, improves upon traditional approaches by significantly reducing noise and excited-state contamination, leading to more precise results, especially at higher hadron momenta.
AI.motivation: The motivation behind this paper is to address the limitations faced in extracting nonlocal correlation functions from lattice QCD calculations, specifically the poor signal-to-noise ratio and excited-state contamination as Euclidean separation and hadron momentum increase. The authors aim to develop a method that can overcome these issues, thereby improving the precision and reliability of the extracted parton distribution functions (PDFs), generalized parton distributions (GPDs), and transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions (TMDPDFs).
AI.method: The paper introduces a novel fitting strategy where the ratio of nonlocal to local correlators is used. This approach aims to project out the dominant ground-state dynamics while minimizing the impact of excited states and noise. It is demonstrated through its application to quark and gluon PDFs, quark GPDs, and TMDPDFs, showing how it simplifies the analysis procedure, particularly for nonforward matrix elements like GPDs. The method is versatile, applying to various Dirac and momentum structures, and both connected and disconnected contributions, making it suitable for integration into existing lattice QCD programs.
AI.result: The results indicate that the proposed method achieves consistency with those obtained from conventional three-point/two-point ratio fits but with significantly enhanced precision and stability. Additionally, the accessible range of hadron momenta is extended. For nonforward matrix elements, the analysis procedure is greatly simplified. The overall improvement in accuracy and the ability to reach larger momenta suggest a valuable advancement in the field of lattice QCD and parton physics studies.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion drawn from the study is that the new fitting strategy offers a significant improvement over traditional methods in terms of precision, stability, and the ability to handle larger hadron momenta in lattice QCD calculations. It is highlighted as an immediately deployable technique within current lattice QCD programs, promising to advance the accuracy and scope of research into hadron structure.

title: Weak (quasi-)PDFs from the lattice
summary: Future colliders will be able to probe the electroweak substructure of particles. An accurate description of this substructure may necessitate electroweak PDFs, similarly to QCD. We investigate therefore the Higgs and W/Z PDFs in a reduced Standard Model setup using lattice methods, determining the quasi-PDFs, and, to lowest order, the resulting PDFs. While uncertainties remain, the results show interesting structures in line with expectations from gauge invariance.

AI.tldr: The study explores the electroweak substructure of particles, particularly focusing on Higgs and W/Z bosons, using lattice methods to determine quasi-PDFs and, to the lowest order, the resulting PDFs. The findings align with expectations from gauge invariance, though uncertainties are present.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to provide an accurate description of the electroweak substructure of particles for future collider experiments, as it may be necessary to use electroweak parton distribution functions (PDFs) similar to those used in QCD.
AI.method: Lattice methods are employed to investigate the Higgs and W/Z boson PDFs within a simplified Standard Model framework. This includes the determination of quasi-PDFs and, at the lowest order, the corresponding PDFs.
AI.result: The results reveal structures that are consistent with the predictions based on gauge invariance, although there are still some uncertainties associated with the analysis.
AI.conclusion: The research concludes that while there are remaining uncertainties, the observed structures in the electroweak PDFs are in agreement with theoretical expectations, indicating the potential importance of electroweak PDFs for future particle physics studies.

title: Complex potential and the thermal width of quarkonium in quark-gluon plasma
summary: We study the complex heavy quark anti-quark potential in lattice 2+1 flavor QCD at non-zero temperature. We point out a close relation between the imaginary part of the potential and the thermal quarkonium width. Using this relation, we estimate the thermal width of charmonia and bottomonia at high temperatures, which are not yet accessible with direct lattice QCD calculations of the quarkonium correlation functions and compare these to the results of the T-matrix analysis. For some of the excited quarkonia states, our estimates of the thermal width are smaller than the ones obtained in the T-matrix analysis.

AI.tldr: The paper explores the complex heavy quark-antiquark potential in lattice QCD at non-zero temperature, relating the imaginary part of the potential to the thermal quarkonium width. The authors estimate and compare the thermal widths of charmonia and bottomonia with T-matrix analysis results, finding some discrepancies for excited states.
AI.motivation: To understand the behavior of heavy quark-antiquark pairs (quarkonia) in a hot QCD medium, which is relevant for the study of heavy ion collisions and the properties of matter under extreme conditions. The motivation also includes improving the estimation of the thermal width of quarkonia, which is a measure of their stability in a thermal bath, since direct calculations are not feasible at high temperatures.
AI.method: The researchers use lattice Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) simulations with 2+1 flavors to compute the complex heavy quark-antiquark potential at non-zero temperature. They establish a connection between the imaginary part of this potential and the thermal width of quarkonia. Using this relationship, they make estimates of the thermal width for charmonia and bottomonia, and then compare these with outcomes from a T-matrix analysis.
AI.result: The estimated thermal widths for charmonia and bottomonia using the established relation are found to be generally smaller than those obtained by T-matrix analysis, particularly for some excited quarkonia states. This suggests that the stability of these particles in a thermal environment may be higher than previously thought, or that there are limitations in the T-matrix approach when applied to certain states.
AI.conclusion: The work provides new insights into the thermal properties of heavy quarkonia in a hot QCD medium, offering an alternative method to estimate their thermal widths. The comparison with T-matrix results indicates a need for further investigation into the dynamics of excited quarkonia states and the validity of different theoretical approaches in this context.
